summary: This experimental RFC, published on April 1, is humorous. It proposes hiding services from clients using the Domain Pseudonym System, a play on service discovery. It is satire.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6593 is an April 1st joke about services hiding from service discovery. It describes a pretend game in which a client waits, guesses, and receives hints from a hidden service.

subtitle: An April 1st joke about hiding services from discovery.

tldr.problem: This April 1st joke imagines service discovery overwhelming clients with advertised services and some services preferring to stay hidden.
tldr.mechanism: Its Domain Pseudonym System uses hiding names, a counting rule, timeouts, and hints that let a seeker guess which service is available.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6593 is an Experimental joke document published on April 1, 2012.

today: RFC 6593 is Experimental and dated April 1, 2012. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Domain Pseudonym System
sections.content: RFC 6593 is an April 1st joke document proposing the Domain Pseudonym System (DPS) for services that do not want to be discovered. A client looking for a service is called the seeker or “it”; the concealed service is the hider. The hider may use a fictitious or facetious name instead of advertising its service directly.
sections.plainLanguage: This April 1st joke gives a hidden service a false name. The client searching for it is called the seeker.

sections.title: Counting, Hiding, and Timeout
sections.content: The seeker counts one step at a time toward a default Count to Live for IPv4 or Count Limit for IPv6 of 50. A hider may change its name while the seeker is not looking, decrementing the count. A seeker that peeks early is placed in a timeout state and denied access to services until the hider decides it has learned its lesson.
sections.plainLanguage: The seeker is supposed to count to 50 before looking. If it looks too soon, the pretend system puts it in timeout.

sections.title: Hints and Guesses
sections.content: A hider may answer a service-list request with GUESS instead of a list. The seeker can then send HINT-REQUEST messages naming services, and the hider replies with temperature-style hints such as WARM or COLD. The seeker may guess up to 20 times before it must reset the count to guess again.
sections.plainLanguage: The hider may give a hint instead of listing its services. The seeker can make up to 20 guesses before resetting its count.
